extracted.intended_audience: staff and advocates at community health centers (CHCs), migrant health centers (MHCs), health care for the homeless (HCH) programs, public housing primary care (PHPC), Primary Care Associations (PCAs), and Health Center Controlled Networks (HCCNs) preparing regulatory comments
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and submitting notice-and-comment letters on proposed health center regulations (especially Section 330 / HRSA-related rules) using NACHC templates, customizing with center-specific and state-specific data and program references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify your health center type
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify your health center type (CHC, MHC, HCH, PHPC, PCA, HCCN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly which program type you represent at the top of the comment so reviewers understand the statutory/regulatory context and applicability; templates reserve space for this identification. If you represent multiple types or an association, specify scope and membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific Section 330 statute provisions and Compliance Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific Section 330 statute provisions and Compliance Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference exact statutory citations and relevant Compliance Manual sections when arguing how a proposal interacts with or alters statutory/regulatory requirements. Use precise citations to strengthen legal/administrative arguments and to guide agency reviewers to applicable authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide patient population data (numbers served, demographics, conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide patient population data (numbers served, demographics, conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete, center-level data on patient counts, breakdowns by age/race/ethnicity/language/insurance status, and prevalent conditions to illustrate how the proposed rule would affect real patients. Templates leave space for local population data; use organization-specific statistics rather than generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address rural/urban access dimensions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how access differs by geography and how the proposal would affect service availability in rural vs. urban settings. Provide examples such as travel distances, provider shortages, or transportation barriers relevant to your service area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with FQHC reimbursement methodologies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how proposed changes affect prospective or retrospective payment methodologies (e.g., Prospective Payment System), revenue streams, billing, and financial sustainability. Use concrete fiscal estimates or examples when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite UDS (Uniform Data System) outcomes data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite UDS (Uniform Data System) outcomes data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available, reference UDS metrics to document service volume, quality measures and outcomes. Use UDS figures to support claims about patient needs, performance, or impacts of a proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address sliding fee scale and underinsured/uninsured populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Address sliding fee scale and underinsured/uninsured populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how rule changes would affect ability to provide sliding fee discounts and care for underinsured/uninsured patients. Include data on uninsured/underinsured patient volumes and financial impacts if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference HRSA program guidance and program assistance letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference HRSA program guidance and program assistance letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant HRSA guidance documents and program assistance letters to show alignment or conflict with proposed regulatory changes. Point to past HRSA interpretations to support your position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with 340B Drug Pricing Program implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with 340B Drug Pricing Program implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposal affects participation in or benefits from the 340B program, including access to medications and resulting financial/clinical impacts. Provide concrete examples of pharmacy/medication access consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address workforce shortage and recruitment challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Address workforce shortage and recruitment challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe local and regional workforce constraints (e.g., clinician shortages, recruitment/retention issues), how the proposal would exacerbate or alleviate those challenges, and any workforce-related costs or programmatic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Medicaid managed care interactions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed rule interacts with Medicaid managed care arrangements in your state(s), including payment flows, contract implications, prior authorization, and network adequacy. Use state-specific examples where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Section 1115 waiver implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, discuss how state Section 1115 demonstration waivers affect implementation of the proposal and patient access, including any waiver-specific policies that would interact with the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite state Medicaid program differences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight variation across states in Medicaid eligibility, benefits, payment, and administration that would affect how a federal proposal plays out locally. Provide examples from your state and, if relevant, contrast with other states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific health center identification (template customization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates leave space for specific health center identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the template fields to insert your center's legal name, service sites, and role (e.g., look-alike vs. federally qualified health center). Clear identification helps the agency catalog and weight comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local population data (template customization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates leave space for local population data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize templates with locality-specific statistics and anecdotes to make comments concrete and place-based. Don’t rely only on national-level statements—demonstrate local impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-specific Medicaid program details (template customization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates leave space for state-specific Medicaid program details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert state policy nuances, waiver items, or managed care arrangements that alter how the rule would affect patients/services in your state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular service line impacts (template customization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates leave space for particular service line impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe effects on specific clinical services (e.g., behavioral health, dental, telehealth, reproductive health) and operational or financial consequences for those lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce considerations (template customization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates leave space for workforce considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize with recruitment/retention data, training needs, credentialing or scope-of-practice issues, and how the rule would affect staffing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality outcomes data (template customization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates leave space for quality outcomes data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert center-specific quality or outcome metrics (beyond UDS if available) to support claims about the impact of proposed changes on care quality.
